messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED PAGE fired for service=redwood-inference.api metric=p99_latency region=us-east threshold=1000ms value=1287ms -- runbooks: /runbooks/latency-slo-burn :rotating_light:
jane_oncall: acked. i'm on it. seeing p99 spike across inference-rt and sidecar routing. initial thought: kv-cache evictions? :thinking_face:
miguel_ops: pulling metrics. k8s HPA looks healthy, but GPU pool queues are backing up. logs show repeated 'kv cache miss' for model=redwood-7b at ~12:37 UTC. snippet: `kv_cache.get(key) -> MISS 472ms`
sara_ops: noticed a deploy about ~12:28 by tim_platform -- can we confirm? not saying it's causal but worth checking rollout history.
tim_platform: confirmed small config rollout (sidecar reconcile) at 12:27 UTC to 4 clusters. It was a traffic-only patch (connection pooling tweak). rolling back now to rule it out.
jane_oncall: good. can we scale dedicated pool for p99 hot shards temporarily? miguel, can you bump pool-dedicated-infer by +2 GPUs in us-east?
miguel_ops: doing `k8s scale deployment/pool-dedicated-infer --replicas=6` now. ETA ~90s. also enabling additional batch workers: `infractl workers add --pool=high-prio --count=3`.
incident-bot: update: autoscaler activity detected; replicas -> 6 (trigger=manual)
ella_custsuccess: any customer-facing impact? CS ticket queue flagged a small uptick in timeouts for a Fortune50 customer. They reported degraded latencies in last 20m.
sara_ops: checking error budget impact. current SLO burn: 12% over 1h window, p99 exceeded. customer timeout rate ~0.6% (above alert threshold). recommend informing CS.
jane_oncall: @ella_custsuccess please notify the customer we are investigating and temporarily scaling capacity. say ETA 15-30m for mitigation. message: "We're investigating increased latency; temporarily scaling capacity and rolling back a recent sidecar tweak. We'll follow up in 30 minutes"
ella_custsuccess: will send that now.
miguel_ops: pool scaling completed. tail p99 dropped from 1287->1120ms in first 60s. still above 1000. collecting flamegraphs and KV cache stats.
tim_platform: rollback completed across 4 clusters. no errors during rollback. monitoring heatmap to see if routing restores.
jane_oncall: good. run quick KV cache warmup: enqueue warmup job for hot prefixes for redwood-7b with `jobs/warmup --model redwood-7b --top=1000`. miguel, kick it off.
miguel_ops: warmup started. logs show concurrent fills at ~12:40.
incident-bot: notable metric: kv_cache_fill_rate increased 8x after warmup job kicked off. p99 partial improvement observed.
sara_ops: recommending we also enable fallback-model routing (lower-capacity but faster quantized variant) for non-critical routes to preserve SLO. that can reduce p99 approx 150-250ms based on prior runs.
jane_oncall: agree. tim, can you enable model-fallback policy for prod-routes tagged low-latency-tolerant?
tim_platform: enabling now: `routingctl set-fallback --tag low-latency-tolerant --variant=redwood-7b-quant`. applied to 12 routes; will ramp 10% -> 50% over 5m.
ella_custsuccess: CS confirms they prefer degraded quality over timeouts for that customer. they want fallback on for their org.
miguel_ops: ramp notes: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 15m. starting ramp step 1.
incident-bot: pagerduty: page acknowledged by jane_oncall at 12:39 UTC; incident state=investigating
jane_oncall: monitoring: p99 now ~950-1100 in rolling 1min windows; variability high. still watching for <1000 consistently.
sara_ops: impact window estimate: began ~12:26 UTC, customers affected ~12:30-12:46; recommend post-incident message and customer impact summary after stabilization.
jane_oncall: next, I'm going to create a short mitigation playbook in the incident doc: - scale dedicated pool + warmup - rollback sidecar patch - enable model-fallback for tolerant routes - hold autoscaler thresholds steady to avoid flapping
tim_platform: note: we should not revert autoscaler changes if we see scaling behaviour; prefer manual control during the incident.
miguel_ops: p99 dropped below 1000ms at 12:49 after warmup + fallback ramp at 50%. marking mitigation successful.
ella_custsuccess: sent follow-up to customer: "Mitigation applied; we're seeing latencies return to normal. We'll send a detailed post-mortem." they replied thanks and asked for ETA on RCA.
jane_oncall: assigning action items: miguel: collect KV cache hit/miss aggregate and warmup timing; tim: audit sidecar rollout and config diff; sara: draft incident summary and SLO impact numbers; ella: manage customer comms and follow-up. I'll hand off after 30m for rotation.
incident-bot: escalation window will auto-close in 40m if no new pages.
jane_oncall: handing off to miguel_ops for next 30m watch. miguel, take lead; i'm offline at 13:30 UTC.
miguel_ops: taking lead. will post updates every 10m or on any regressions.
sara_ops: thanks team. quick retro note: consider adding a pre-warm job as part of rollout jobs for sidecar changes that touch routing timeouts.
jane_oncall: agreed. also suggest a playbook card: "SLO burn heatmap -> immediate warmup -> fallback ramp" so oncall has clear steps.
miguel_ops: copying logs and metrics into incident doc now.
incident-bot: incident resolved? No active pages. last recorded p99 within SLO for 10m. state=monitored.
ella_custsuccess: customer follow-up sent with provisional RCA ETA 48h.
jane_oncall: closing oncall notes here. will convert to postmortem ticket. thanks everyone. :bow:
